concepts.name: Turns and the final direction
concepts.description: Right is a quarter turn clockwise and left a quarter turn anticlockwise, whichever way you face; add the turns as angles.

concepts.name: Shortest distance from the start
concepts.description: Add up the east–west and the north–south movement separately, then use Pythagoras.

concepts.name: Where one point lies from another
concepts.description: The signs of the net east and north movement name the direction: north-east, south-west and so on.

concepts.name: Shadows and the sun
concepts.description: The sun rises in the east, so morning shadows point west and evening shadows point east.

formulas.title: Compass and turns
formulas.prompt: Facing south, which way do you face after turning right?
formulas.formula:
Clockwise: N → NE → E → SE → S → SW → W → NW → N (45° each)
Right = 90° clockwise, left = 90° anticlockwise, about turn = 180°
formulas.explanation: Left and right belong to the walker, not to the page: turn the compass, not the paper.
formulas.example: Facing south and turning right: S + 90° clockwise = west.
formulas.commonMistake: Turning by the page: a right turn while facing south is west, not east.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Facing west, Ravi turns left. Which way does he face?

formulas.title: Net movement
formulas.prompt: How do you find where a walker ends up after several legs?
formulas.formula:
Net east = east legs − west legs
Net north = north legs − south legs
formulas.explanation: Only the totals along each line matter; the order of the legs does not change the end point.
formulas.example: 5 km N, 3 km E, 9 km S, 1 km W: net 2 km east, 4 km south.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding every leg, which gives the distance walked, not the position.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A walker goes 6 km E, 2 km N, 10 km W. Where is she from the start?

formulas.title: Shortest distance
formulas.prompt: A walker ends x km east and y km north of the start. How far away is she?
formulas.explanation: The two net movements are the sides of a right-angled triangle; the way back is its hypotenuse.
formulas.example: 6 km east and 8 km north: √(36 + 64) = 10 km.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding x and y instead of using Pythagoras.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A cyclist ends 5 km west and 12 km south of the start. How far is she from it?

formulas.title: Direction from the start
formulas.prompt: How do you name the direction of the end point from the start?
formulas.formula:
North or south from the sign of the net north movement
East or west from the sign of the net east movement
Both non-zero: north-east, north-west, south-east or south-west
formulas.explanation: Exams name the quadrant (north-east and so on) unless the point lies exactly on a line.
formulas.example: Net 3 km east and 4 km south: south-east of the start. The start is north-west of the walker.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering where the start is from the walker when asked the reverse.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Q is 5 km west and 2 km north of P. In which direction is P from Q?

formulas.title: Shadows
formulas.prompt: Which way does a shadow point in the morning, and in the evening?
formulas.formula:
Morning: sun in the east → shadow points west
Evening: sun in the west → shadow points east
formulas.explanation: A shadow always points away from the sun. (Around noon in India the sun is high, so questions use morning or evening.)
formulas.example: In the morning your shadow falls to your left: west is on your left, so you face north.
formulas.commonMistake: Pointing the shadow towards the sun.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In the evening, Meena’s shadow falls behind her. Which way does she face?

formulas.title: Count the turns
formulas.prompt: How can you find the final facing after many turns without tracking each one?
formulas.formula:
Count right turns +1 and left turns −1 (about turn = 2)
Net ÷ 4: the remainder 0, 1, 2, 3 = same, right, about, left
formulas.explanation: Four right turns bring you back, so only the net count matters.
formulas.example: Facing east: R, R, L, R, L, L, L → +1 +1 −1 +1 −1 −1 −1 = −1, one left turn: north.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Facing north: L, L, R, L. Which way now?

formulas.title: Right-angle triples
formulas.prompt: Which right-angled triangles have whole-number sides?
formulas.explanation: Exam routes are built on these, so a net movement of 9 and 12 means the answer is 15.
formulas.example: 12 km east, 5 km north: 5, 12, 13, so 13 km.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Net 15 km south and 8 km west: how far?

levels.title: Which Way Now?
levels.description: Turns, the way back, and shadows.

blocks.title: Turn like the walker, not the page
blocks.body: Right is always a quarter turn clockwise and left a quarter turn anticlockwise, from wherever the walker is facing. Facing south, a right turn points west. Keep a compass in the corner of your sketch and turn the arrow, not the paper.

blocks.title: Eight directions, 45° apart
blocks.body:
N → NE → E → SE → S → SW → W → NW → N  (clockwise)
Right = +90°   Left = −90°   About turn = 180°
blocks.caption: Add the turns as angles; the net angle from the start direction gives the final facing.

blocks.title: The way back is a hypotenuse
blocks.body: To find how far the walker is from the start, add the movement along each line separately: east minus west, north minus south. The two totals are the sides of a right-angled triangle, and the straight way back is its long side: √(x² + y²). The signs of the totals name the direction: 3 km east and 4 km south is 5 km south-east.

blocks.title: A worked route
blocks.body: Ravi walks 6 km north, turns right and walks 8 km. Net: 8 km east, 6 km north. Distance √(64 + 36) = 10 km, to the north-east of the start. The start is south-west of Ravi.
Shadows: the sun rises in the east, so a morning shadow points west and an evening shadow points east. Put the shadow on the side the question says, then read off the way the person faces.

levels.title: Compass Rules
levels.description: Turns, net movement, Pythagoras, directions and shadows.

levels.title: Single Turns and Short Walks
levels.description: One or two turns, two-leg walks and simple shadows.

levels.title: Longer Routes
levels.description: Several legs, about turns, positions of places and two people facing each other.

levels.title: Routes, Places and Big Turns
levels.description: Five-leg routes, distance with direction, two walkers and turns past a full circle.

questions.question: Arjun stands facing north. He turns right, then turns right again, then turns left. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Right from north is east; right again is south; left from south is east. Net: one right turn, so east.
questions.method: Turn the compass arrow one quarter at a time, or count R = +1, L = −1.

hints.text: A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise from wherever he faces.
Two rights and one left leave one right turn in all.

commonMistakes: Turning left as if he were still facing north (answering west).

questions.question: Meena is facing west. She turns 135° clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from west: 45° to north-west, 90° to north, 135° to north-east.
solutionSteps: 135° = 3 points clockwise from west: NW, N, NE.
questions.method: Count compass points: 45° each.

hints.text: How many 45° steps make 135°?
Step clockwise from west: north-west, north, ...

commonMistakes: Turning anticlockwise (south-east).
Counting 135° as two points (north).

questions.question: Ravi walks 6 km north, then turns right and walks 8 km. How far is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing north, a right turn points east. So Ravi is 6 km north and 8 km east of the start: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km.
questions.method: The two legs are at right angles: use Pythagoras.

hints.text: Which direction does he walk after turning right from north?
The two legs form a right angle. 6, 8, ...?

commonMistakes: Adding the legs (14 km): that is the distance walked.

questions.question: Early one morning, Kavya stands in a field and sees her shadow straight in front of her. Which direction is she facing?
questions.explanation: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows point west. The shadow is in front of her, so she faces west.
solutionSteps: Shadow in front of her: she faces west.
questions.method: Shadows point away from the sun.

hints.text: Where is the sun early in the morning?
A shadow points away from the sun.

commonMistakes: Facing the sun (east) instead of the shadow.

questions.question: Suresh walks 5 km south, then turns left and walks 3 km. In which direction is he now from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing south, a left turn points east. So Suresh is 5 km south and 3 km east of the start: south-east.
questions.method: Find the net north–south and east–west movement, then name the quadrant.

hints.text: Facing south, which way is your left hand?
He is south of the start and ... of it.

commonMistakes: Taking left as west, as it would be when facing north.

questions.question: Lata is facing south-east. She turns 90° clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from south-east: 45° to south, 90° to south-west.
questions.method: Count compass points clockwise.

hints.text: 90° is two steps of 45°.
From south-east, the next point clockwise is south.

commonMistakes: Turning anticlockwise (north-east).

questions.question: One evening, Imran stands in an open ground and notices that his shadow falls exactly to his right. Which direction is he facing?
questions.explanation: In the evening the sun is in the west, so shadows point east. With east on his right, Imran faces north.
solutionSteps: East on his right means he faces north.
questions.method: Place the shadow, then turn yourself to match.

hints.text: Where does an evening shadow point?
Facing which way is east on your right?

commonMistakes: Using the morning rule (shadow to the west), which gives south.

questions.question: Priya walks 9 km east, then turns left and walks 5 km, then turns left and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 3 km. How many kilometres is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: East 9; left from east is north, 5; left from north is west, 3; right from west is north, 3. Net: 9 − 3 = 6 km east and 5 + 3 = 8 km north. Distance √(36 + 64) = 10 km.
questions.method: Net east and net north, then Pythagoras.

hints.text: Sketch it: a dot for the start, north up the page, each leg drawn in turn.
Add the north legs; subtract the west leg from the east leg.

commonMistakes: Adding all four legs (20 km).
Turning right from west to south.

questions.question: Gopal walks 4 km west, then turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right and walks 9 km, then turns right and walks 2 km. In which direction is he now from his starting point?
questions.explanation: West 4; right from west is north, 6; right from north is east, 9; right from east is south, 2. Net: 9 − 4 = 5 km east, 6 − 2 = 4 km north. He is north-east of the start.
questions.method: Signs of the net movement name the direction.

hints.text: Sketch it: a dot for the start, north up the page, each leg drawn in turn.
Is he east or west of the start at the end? North or south?

commonMistakes: Answering with the last direction walked (south).

questions.question: Deepa walks 12 km north, then turns back and walks 7 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. How far is she from where she started?
questions.explanation: Turning back from north, she walks 7 km south, so she is 5 km north of the start. Facing south, left is east: 12 km east. Distance √(5² + 12²) = 13 km.
solutionSteps: 12 N then 7 S: net 5 km north.
Facing south, left = east: 12 km east.
questions.method: After an about turn, left and right swap compared with the original facing.

hints.text: After turning back she faces south. Which way is her left now?
Net north is 12 − 7. Then use 5, 12, ...

commonMistakes: Forgetting that after the about turn she faces south, so her left is east.
Using 12 and 12 as the sides of the triangle.

questions.question: Anita is facing north. She turns 90° clockwise, then turns 225° anticlockwise, then turns 45° clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: Net turn: +90 − 225 + 45 = −90°, that is 90° anticlockwise. From north, 90° anticlockwise is west.
questions.method: Add the angles with signs, turn once.

hints.text: Give clockwise turns a + sign and anticlockwise turns a − sign.
The net turn is 90° one way.

commonMistakes: Adding all the angles as if they were the same way (360°, back to north).

questions.question: One morning, Vikram and Sunita stand talking, facing each other. Vikram notices that his shadow falls exactly to his right. Which direction is Sunita facing?
questions.explanation: Morning shadows point west. West is on Vikram’s right, so he faces south. Sunita faces him, so she faces north.
solutionSteps: West on his right: Vikram faces south.
Facing each other: Sunita faces north.
questions.method: Settle the first person’s facing from the shadow, then turn round for the other.

hints.text: Which way does Vikram face if west is on his right?
Two people facing each other face opposite directions.

commonMistakes: Answering Vikram’s direction (south) instead of Sunita’s.

questions.question: Village P is 6 km north of Q, and village R is 8 km east of Q. How far, and in which direction, is R from P?
questions.explanation: Put Q at the origin: P is at (0, 6), R at (8, 0). From P to R: 8 km east and 6 km south, so √(64 + 36) = 10 km, to the south-east.
questions.method: Place the points on axes, then go from the first-named point to the other.

hints.text: Draw Q, then P straight above it and R to its right.
Is R north or south of P? East or west?

commonMistakes: Giving the direction of P from R (north-west).
Adding 6 and 8.

questions.question: Mohan is facing north. Which of these sequences of turns leave him facing west? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: West is 90° anticlockwise (or 270° clockwise) from north. Left: −90° ✓. Three rights: +270° ✓. About turn then left: 180° − 90° = +90°, east ✗. 135° + 45° = 180°, south ✗. Two 45° anticlockwise turns: −90° ✓.
solutionSteps: The first, second and fifth work.
questions.method: Reduce each sequence to one net angle.

hints.text: Write each sequence as a net angle, clockwise positive.
Three right turns equal one left turn.

commonMistakes: Treating "about turn, then left" as west (after an about turn he faces south; left from south is east).

questions.question: Uma walks 3 km north, then turns right and walks 2 km, then turns right and walks 7 km, then turns left and walks 4 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: Directions: N 3, E 2, S 7, E 4, S 4. Net east 2 + 4 = 6; net south 7 + 4 − 3 = 8. Distance √(36 + 64) = 10 km.
solutionSteps: Facings: north, east, south, east, south.
questions.method: Write each leg as a compass direction first; only then add.

hints.text: Sketch it: a dot for the start, north up the page, each leg drawn in turn.
After "right, right" she faces south; a left from south is east.

commonMistakes: Taking the left turn from south as west.

questions.question: Kiran cycles 9 km south, then turns left and cycles 8 km, then turns right and cycles 6 km. How far, and in which direction, is Kiran from the starting point?
questions.explanation: South 9; left from south is east, 8; right from east is south, 6. Net: 8 km east, 15 km south. √(64 + 225) = 17 km, south-east.
questions.method: Net movement, then Pythagoras and the quadrant.

hints.text: Facing south, which way is left?
Net south is 9 + 6. Then 8, 15, ...

commonMistakes: Adding the legs (23 km).
Taking left from south as west (south-west).

questions.question: Asha and Bhanu start from the same point. Asha walks 7 km east. Bhanu walks 4 km north, then turns right and walks 4 km. How far, and in which direction, is Asha from Bhanu now?
questions.explanation: Asha is at (7, 0). Bhanu: 4 north, then right (east) 4, so at (4, 4). From Bhanu to Asha: 3 km east, 4 km south: 5 km, south-east.
questions.method: Give both people coordinates from the common start, then subtract.

hints.text: Where does each of them end up, as (east, north)?
Asha minus Bhanu: how far east, how far south?

commonMistakes: Answering Bhanu’s direction from Asha (north-west).

questions.question: Just after sunrise, Pooja walks 2 km towards her shadow, then turns left and walks 1 km. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation: Just after sunrise the sun is in the east, so her shadow points west and she walks west. Facing west, a left turn points south.
solutionSteps: Morning shadow: west, so she first faces west.
questions.method: Shadow first, then the turns.

hints.text: Which way does her shadow point just after sunrise?
Facing west, where is your left hand?

commonMistakes: Walking towards the sun (east), which gives north.

questions.question: Prakash is facing east. He turns 1035° clockwise on the spot. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Full turns change nothing: 1035 = 2 × 360 + 315. A 315° clockwise turn is the same as 45° anticlockwise. From east, 45° anticlockwise is north-east.
questions.method: Remove whole turns of 360°, then turn the rest.

hints.text: Subtract 360° as many times as you can.
315° clockwise is how much anticlockwise?

commonMistakes: Turning 45° clockwise instead of anticlockwise (south-east).

questions.question: A school bus goes 12 km north from the depot, then turns right and goes 10 km, then turns right and goes 4 km, then turns left and goes 5 km. How many kilometres is it from the depot (in a straight line)?
questions.explanation: North 12; right from north is east, 10; right from east is south, 4; left from south is east, 5. Net: 15 km east, 8 km north. √(225 + 64) = 17 km.
questions.method: Net east and net north, then Pythagoras.

hints.text: Sketch it: a dot for the start, north up the page, each leg drawn in turn.
Net north is 12 − 4; net east is 10 + 5.

commonMistakes: Adding all the legs (31 km).
Taking left from south as west.

questions.question: Point A is 4 m west of B, and point C is 4 m north of B. In which direction is A from C?
questions.explanation: Put B at the origin: A (−4, 0), C (0, 4). From C to A: 4 m west and 4 m south, so A is south-west of C.
questions.method: Coordinates from a common point, then "target minus reference".

hints.text: Place B at the centre of your sketch.
Start at C and walk to A: which way do you go?

commonMistakes: Giving C’s direction from A (north-east).
